name: Next Generation Diabetes Drugs
blurb: Triple agonists, amylin combinations and new oral GLP-1 pills.
title: Next Generation Diabetes Drugs
answer: The next wave acts on more than one hormone at once. Retatrutide targets GLP-1, GIP and glucagon receptors; amylin combinations pair a GLP-1 drug with an amylin analogue; and small molecule pills such as orforglipron deliver GLP-1 effects without injections or fasting rules. Only orforglipron is approved so far, and only for weight management.

sections.heading: What it means for patients

siblings.name: Kidney Protection and Diabetic Kidney Disease

explainer:
Adding hormones increases the effect. Glucagon, best known for raising blood sugar, also increases energy use and affects fat in the liver, so a drug that combines it with GLP-1 and GIP can drive weight loss beyond either alone while the incretin effects keep glucose in check. Amylin, released with insulin by beta cells, slows stomach emptying and increases fullness; combining an amylin analogue with a GLP-1 drug, as in Novo Nordisk's CagriSema or Lilly's EloraTZP, adds a second appetite signal.

Oral small molecules are the other frontier. Earlier oral semaglutide must be taken on an empty stomach with little water, 30 minutes before food. Orforglipron is a non-peptide molecule that avoids those rules. The trade off across the next generation is tolerability: greater effect usually brings more gastrointestinal side effects and more people stopping treatment.

developments.text: In the phase 3 TRIUMPH-2 trial in people with obesity and type 2 diabetes, retatrutide 12 mg produced 20.8 percent average weight loss over 80 weeks. It is not approved.
EloraTZP produced up to 23.3 percent weight loss and a 2.9 point A1C drop over 48 weeks in type 2 diabetes in a phase 2b trial, with phase 3 planned for late 2026.
The FDA approved Foundayo (orforglipron) for weight management, the first GLP-1 pill that can be taken any time of day without food or water rules.
